explainedBy: Information takes time to arrive: Meadows introduces the time lag (clock) between an event and our reaction.

storyboard.claim: Real-world information does not travel instantly; systems have delays.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella Meadows beside a clock: time passing between cause and reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the feedback loops to their flaw: delay.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock makes "delay" a matter of time, not a mood.

explainedBy: The car dealer paces her lot with her clipboard: the person who will live the delay story.

storyboard.claim: Picture a panicking car dealership manager pacing a sunbaked lot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer in her blazer walking the lot, clipboard in hand, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the dealer story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the dealer and her anxiety physically (pacing).

explainedBy: A customer with money in hand faces the dealer who has no cars to sell: demand meets an empty lot.
noVisual: Empty parking spaces cannot be drawn; the customer with cash carries the demand side.

storyboard.claim: Customers walk in with cash, but the lot is empty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A customer holding his wallet, cash beside him, in front of the worried dealer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the customer to the dealer stage.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: shows the demand (cash) but not the empty rows.

explainedBy: The dealer slumps because the factory that should supply her cars is backed up: supply cannot follow demand.

storyboard.claim: They want cars today, but the factory is backed up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The factory icon beside the slumping dealer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the eager customer to the stuck supplier.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names where the cars come from and why they are missing.

explainedBy: The dealer stares at her clipboard, averaging five days of sales before she orders, sweating as profits slip away.

storyboard.claim: She averages the last 5 days of sales before ordering, losing profits each day she waits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer holding her clipboard, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same dealer; the factory leaves, the clipboard comes up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the deciding tool (clipboard of sales).

explainedBy: The dealer, clipboard in hand, stands beside a clock: her system is ruled by time lags.

storyboard.claim: The dealer is trapped in a system defined by delays, which cause oscillations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock appears beside the worried dealer with her clipboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same dealer and clipboard; the clock joins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links her trouble to time lags.

explainedBy: The first of three delays: her clipboard average of 5 days of sales is how she perceives demand.

storyboard.claim: She faces three delays; first, a perception delay from averaging 5 days of sales.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer reading her clipboard of sales numbers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same dealer; the clock goes, the first named delay appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the perception delay to the clipboard she reads.

explainedBy: She reacts to the averaged past on her clipboard, not to yesterday's true demand.

storyboard.claim: She reacts to a smoothed-out past, not to real demand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer staring blankly at her clipboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the face goes blank on old numbers.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the lag lives in the label; the clipboard shows what she reads.

explainedBy: The three delays in order: noticing demand, acting on it, then the cars actually arriving.

storyboard.claim: Second a response delay (paperwork, approval, ordering); third, the delivery delay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow of the dealer's delays.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the list of three delays as one chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows all three delays and their order at once.

explainedBy: The factory takes weeks or months to build and ship cars to her lot: the longest delay.

storyboard.claim: Delivery takes weeks or months: steel, building, train, shipping. It is the hotel shower problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The factory beside the slumped dealer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the chain back to its biggest link, the factory.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the delivery delay at the factory.

callout.text: A shower in a cheap hotel

explainedBy: The everyman reaches to turn on a hotel shower: the analogy everyone has lived.

storyboard.claim: You turn on the shower in a cheap hotel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman reaching toward a shower head with a hot/cold knob.
storyboard.onScreenText: A shower in a cheap hotel
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from the dealer to the shower analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the shower setup physically.

explainedBy: The everyman points at the long pipe to the shower head: the water needs time to travel.

storyboard.claim: The pipe from the mixer to the shower head is very long: a delivery delay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same shower; he points at the long pipe.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same shower and man; he now points at the pipe.
storyboard.addedInformation: The icon's long pipe is the delay itself.

explainedBy: He is freezing and reaches to crank the knob to hot, but nothing changes yet.

storyboard.claim: You step in freezing, crank the dial to hot, nothing happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worried man reaching for the shower knob.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; his face turns worried and he reaches for the knob.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the action taken before feedback arrives.

explainedBy: He cranks it to maximum, and ten seconds later the hot water arrives and scalds him.

storyboard.claim: You crank to maximum; seconds later boiling water scalds you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same shower; his face jumps to fear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worry turns to fear as the hot water lands.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the result of over-reacting to a delay.

explainedBy: He slumps under the shower: by the time the feedback reached him he had already acted too much.

storyboard.claim: You overshot because the feedback came after you had already over-adjusted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same shower; the man slumps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; fear gives way to defeat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Closes the analogy: act, wait, overshoot.

explainedBy: Her inventory swings between two extremes, an empty lot and an overflowing lot.

storyboard.claim: Her inventory swings from an empty lot to an overflowing lot; she loses money both ways.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from empty lot to overflowing lot with marks at both ends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back from the shower to the dealer's swinging stock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the oscillation as two extremes.

explainedBy: The tempting fix: the dealer, clipboard in hand, decides to react faster to cut the delay.

storyboard.claim: The logical fix for delays seems to be reacting faster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer with her clipboard, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the swing to the proposed fix.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the fix is carried by the label.

explainedBy: The dealer grabs her phone to order five sedans the moment one customer asks for one.

storyboard.claim: Cut the response delay to 2 days; one request, order five immediately.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer picks up her phone on the cue to place the order.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same dealer; she takes the phone and acts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the over-eager order as a deed.

explainedBy: Meadows holds her book: the text works this scenario out mathematically.

storyboard.claim: No: the book models this scenario mathematically.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella Meadows holding her book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dealer's plan to the author's answer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the source of the counter-argument.

explainedBy: Cause and effect: reacting faster makes the oscillations worse.

storyboard.claim: If she reacts faster, the oscillations get significantly worse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from reacting faster to worse oscillations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the book's counter-intuitive result.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause -> effect directly.

explainedBy: The dealer on her phone is fast, but the factory building the cars is still slow.

storyboard.claim: We love agility, but the factory delivery delay is still slow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer with her phone beside the factory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the dealer: her fast phone versus the slow factory.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts her speed with the factory's.

explainedBy: She orders on a tiny blip; three days pass and the factory has not delivered.

storyboard.claim: Reacting faster she chases her own tail: orders on a blip, cars not arrived after three days.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same dealer with phone and factory, still waiting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; time passes with nothing delivered.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the waiting is in the label.

explainedBy: In a panic the dealer grabs the order sheet and orders more cars, overcorrecting.

storyboard.claim: The lot is still empty; she panics and orders more.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same stage; her face turns to fear, phone in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worry turns to panic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the panic reaction to delayed feedback.

explainedBy: All the orders arrive at once: the dealer slumps over her clipboard as 500 cars hit a lot built for 100.
noVisual: No car icon: the oversupply is carried by the number in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Two months later 500 cars arrive on a lot built for a hundred.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer slumping with her clipboard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From under-ordering panic to overflow.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the overflow is in the number.

explainedBy: After the loss, the lesson: with long delivery delays she must lengthen her response delay and slow down.

storyboard.claim: She slashes prices at a loss; the fix is to slow down her response.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same dealer, sad and slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; defeat, then the lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the counter-intuitive fix.

explainedBy: The dealer sits down beside a clock: she waits longer, 6 or 10 days, before reacting.

storyboard.claim: Lengthen her delay from 3 to 6 or even 10 days; ride out the blips.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The dealer seated with her clipboard beside a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same dealer; she stops pacing and sits, a clock appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows waiting as a physical change (standing -> sitting).

explainedBy: She sits on her hands with her clipboard average and stays calm: slower mental reaction to slow delivery.

storyboard.claim: Sit on your hands and trust the long-term average; slow down your mental reaction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same seated dealer, now calm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worry gone, she waits calmly.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the disciplined result.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: reacting too fast amplifies the chaos into the bullwhip effect.
noVisual: No supply-chain or whip icon; the term is text-led.

storyboard.claim: Otherwise you amplify the chaos: this is the bullwhip effect in global supply chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cause -> effect: reacting too fast amplifies the chaos into the bullwhip effect.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the single dealer to the global pattern. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the name is carried by text.

explainedBy: A laid-off worker walks away with his briefcase: the bust half of the economy's boom and bust.

storyboard.claim: Boom and bust: massive layoffs followed by desperate hiring sprees months later.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sad worker walking out with a briefcase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the bullwhip to jobs.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the human cost of the swing (layoff).

explainedBy: The cause of boom and bust is not foolish managers but reacting too quickly to delayed information.

storyboard.claim: Not foolish managers: managers reacting too quickly to delayed information.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from delayed information to reacting too quickly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the cause behind the layoffs.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the structural cause instead of blaming people.

explainedBy: A runaway snowball growing downhill: the reinforcing loop whose behavior comes from its structure.

storyboard.claim: The behavior is in the structure; we have runaway reinforcing loops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A snowball rolling and growing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recaps the reinforcing loop.
storyboard.addedInformation: The snowball reads as a runaway loop.

explainedBy: The same runaway snowball now heading for a limit: what happens when growth hits a wall.
noVisual: No wall or limit icon; the limit is named in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Runaway loops plus delays: next, what happens when they hit a wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same snowball.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same snowball; the limit is announced.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the wall is text-only.
